definitions.explanation: The polite form of {店|みせ}. Refers to any retail shop, restaurant, or similar establishment. Very commonly used in everyday conversation.

examples.japanese: いいお{店|みせ}を{知|し}っていますか。
examples.english: Do you know a good restaurant?

examples.japanese: {駅前|えきまえ}に{新|あたら}しいお{店|みせ}ができた。
examples.english: A new shop opened in front of the station.

examples.japanese: このお{店|みせ}は{値段|ねだん}も{手頃|てごろ}で、{料理|りょうり}も{美味|おい}しいのでよく{来|く}ます。
examples.english: This restaurant has reasonable prices and good food, so I come here often.

notes:
The polite prefix お attached to {店|みせ} (shop/store). In everyday Japanese, お{店|みせ} is far more common than plain {店|みせ}, especially when speaking. It can refer to any type of commercial establishment — retail shops, restaurants, bars, cafes, etc.

USAGE:
While {店|みせ} on its own can sound blunt, お{店|みせ} is the standard conversational form. Using {店|みせ} without お is more common in compound words ({店員|てんいん}, {店長|てんちょう}) or when used as a suffix ({花屋|はなや}の{店|みせ}).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{店|みせ}を{出|だ}す: to open a shop
- お{店|みせ}を{探|さが}す: to look for a restaurant/shop
- お{店|みせ}の{人|ひと}: shop staff; restaurant staff

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {店舗|てんぽ}: store; shop premises — more formal/commercial
- ショップ: shop — borrowed from English, often for specialty or trendy stores
- {商店|しょうてん}: shop; store — more traditional, often in {商店街|しょうてんがい} (shopping street)
